tasks.short: Collect interconnection and development data for efficiency

steps.what: Export feeder load and interconnection capacity
Read development and population figures

loop.output: development id and the stated total
loop.check: The extracted count equals the total printed in the note
loop.stop: If there is no total, leave the row blank and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: Planning notes do not share one table layout

steps.what: Fill an efficiency ratio only where both inputs exist
Judge operating efficiency from complete rows
Confirm a development or population figure

tasks.design: A job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} pulls feeder id, peak load, annual energy, and interconnection capacity into a {BI} table. Development and population figures that arrive as documents are read once into those fields and checked against the printed total. A ratio is filled only when both inputs exist. The electrical engineer signs which rows are complete enough to judge operating efficiency. This is not an energy filing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Load, interconnection, and planning figures lived in different sheets, so a ratio could not show which source it used.
tasks.enabler_now: An operations export can carry a feeder id, and a planning note can be checked against a printed total.
tasks.still_hard: Many feeders have a missing load, and a complete row still does not say what to change.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer decides which incomplete row is still usable and which efficiency problem is real.

ambition.what: Review efficiency when a new interconnection is added, not only in the yearly study

tasks.altitude: Less time copying loads. The same duty to say what the numbers mean. The engineer can refuse a ratio that used a blank field.

reach.task: Confirm a development figure the table could not check
reach.learn: Which development ids are blank and which totals failed the check

evidence.claim: Operating-efficiency work in a mid-size firm is a spreadsheet of loads plus a few planning figures. The judgement is which rows are complete enough to use.
A missing load or a missing interconnection capacity must stay blank. Filling it with a guess would make the efficiency ratio look finished when it is not.

assumptions: Focal role is the electrical engineer. The task ends at a signed view of which systems look inefficient. Changing a feeder is a later task.
Input contract: feeder id, peak load, annual energy, interconnection capacity, development id, stated planning total. Producer is the operations export and the planner. A blank field stays blank.
Native exports and the dashboard are configured before custom code. The ratio is a fixed division, not a model.
This is not an energy information filing. No statutory threshold is used.
The meeting prior overstates meetings. Most time is the spreadsheet and the planning documents. One confirmation with the planner remains.
unknowns: Whether planning figures are public or come from a customer.
Who may mark a row complete when the engineer is absent.
research_questions: What share of feeders has no annual energy figure?
How often does a planning total disagree with the rows in the note?

already_counted.description: Engineer checks planning figures the read got wrong
Efficiency judgement stays with the engineer

incremental.description: Map a new planning note layout into the field list
Planner corrects a total the check rejected

approvals.approved_version: efficiency view signed for this extract

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes planning figures stay unstructured and many feeders lack a load, so the engineer still builds the table. The high case assumes exports are clean, but every efficiency call stays with the engineer. No corrective project is treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design systems that produce renewable electricity

steps.what: State the site, the source, and the target output
Choose wind, solar, or another source and the protection
Extend the parts list from the catalogue
Copy yield figures from the simulation log

loop.input: simulation log and the run id
loop.output: yield figures that match the log
loop.check: Each yield figure equals the value printed for that run id
loop.stop: If the log has no run id, leave the note blank and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: Log layouts differ, so a fixed cell can copy the wrong figure

steps.what: Review the renewable concept with the customer
Sign the renewable electricity design
File the signed design and parts list

tasks.design: The customer states site id, source, target output, and connection voltage on a {WORKFLOW} form. A {SPREADSHEET} extends a parts list only from catalogue ids the electrical engineer has marked current. A yield figure may be copied from a simulation log into {DOCS}, and only if it matches that log. Protection and trip values are written by the engineer, not proposed by a model. The customer meeting stays a meeting. One signed design version is filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Site notes, catalogue cuts, and yield figures lived in mail, so a parts list could not show which source it used.
tasks.enabler_now: A catalogue can carry a part id, and a simulation log can carry a run id that a figure must match.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the arrangement, and every protection setting, depends on the site and stays with the engineer.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer chooses the source arrangement and every protection setting, and can stop a design the site cannot support.

ambition.what: Re-sign the concept when the target output changes, not only at the first customer meeting

tasks.altitude: The parts list and the yield copy take less rewriting. The concept and the customer meeting do not move. The engineer can refuse a yield figure with no run id.

reach.task: Build only from the signed parts list
reach.learn: Which part ids are signed and which rows were left blank

evidence.claim: Designing a small renewable system in a mid-size firm is a concept, a parts list, and a customer meeting. The concept and the meeting stay with the engineer.
Digest [S11] says an executable simulation call is not a correct result. A yield note may only repeat a figure that is already in the log.
Digest [S12] and [S13] say a safety component in electricity can be high-risk AI, with those duties from 2 December 2027. A model must not set protection or trip values.

assumptions: Focal role is the electrical engineer. The task ends at a signed design version and parts list. Grid permits and construction are later tasks.

Input contract: site id, source type, target output, connection voltage, catalogue part id, simulation run id. Producer of the site fields is the customer. The engineer chooses catalogue ids. A missing catalogue id stays blank.
The parts list uses the spreadsheet and the catalogue first. Custom code only after that fails.
The customer meeting and the concept stay with the person. A yield figure with no run id is not written into the note.
Protection, earthing, and trip settings are written only by the engineer.
unknowns: Whether connection voltage is set by the customer or by the network operator.
Who signs when the design leaves the firm.
Whether this site later needs an energy filing. This task does not file one.
research_questions: What share of parts has no catalogue id?
How often does the customer reject the first concept?

already_counted.description: Concept and protection choices stay with the engineer
Engineer checks yield figures against the log
Customer meeting stays with the engineer

incremental.description: Add catalogue ids when a new source type is offered
Customer resubmits site fields that were incomplete

approvals.approved_version: renewable design version signed for this site
the same signed renewable design version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes the catalogue does not match the source, so the parts list stays manual and only the filing is new. The high case assumes the list and the yield copy work, but the concept, the customer meeting, and the signature stay. Permits are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop software to control electrical systems

steps.what: Mark electrical tags and the safety flag
Draft routine software for tags that are not safety

loop.input: signed tag list and the routine pattern
loop.output: a block that references only non-safety tags
loop.check: Every tag in the block is on the list and marked not safety
loop.stop: If any tag is missing or marked safety, return an empty block and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: Tag names differ by machine, so a fixed library cannot cover them

steps.what: Develop the safety control functions by hand
Run the bench test on the control software
Sign the tested control software version
File the test log for that software version
Load the signed software onto the electrical systems
outputs: control software on the electrical systems

tasks.design: The electrical engineer writes an I/O list in {DOCS} with a tag, a type, and a safety flag. A bounded draft on the {DATA_PLATFORM} may propose routine software only for tags marked not safety, and only if every tag is on the list. Safety functions are written by the engineer. A bench log in {SPREADSHEET} stores pass or fail. Nothing is loaded until that tested version is signed, and the load stays a person at the panel.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tag lists lived in old projects and mail, so a draft could not know which tag was a safety function.
tasks.enabler_now: An I/O list can carry a tag and a safety flag that a draft can be checked against before anyone runs it.
tasks.still_hard: A safety interlock written wrongly can harm someone, and each machine's tags differ.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer marks safety tags, writes those functions, and refuses a load when a test has failed.

ambition.what: Re-test and re-sign after any tag change, not only at the first release

tasks.altitude: Routine non-safety tags may take less typing. Safety code, the bench, and the load do not move. The engineer can refuse a block that touches a safety tag.

reach.task: Load only the software version the engineer signed
reach.learn: Which version passed the bench and which tags are safety

evidence.claim: Control software for electrical equipment is still written and tested by the engineer. A routine block can be drafted only from a signed tag list. Safety functions stay manual.
Digest [S14] says machinery rules cover AI safety functions from 20 January 2027. A generated block must not be the safety function.
Digest [S12] and [S13] say a safety component in electricity can be high-risk AI. The engineer signs the tested version, and a person loads it.

assumptions: Focal role is the electrical engineer. The task runs from the I/O list through a signed test and a person loading that version. An unattended load is out of scope.
Input contract: tag, signal type, safety yes or no, test id, expected result, software version. Producer is the engineer. A tag with no safety flag is treated as safety and is not drafted.
The bench uses the existing rig. Native pass or fail logging is configured before custom code.
The meeting prior is high. On this task the time is the list, the code, and the bench, not a series of meetings. That disagreement is deliberate.
A block marked safety is never drafted. Whether the machine is in scope of the machinery rules is a fact to confirm. The design assumes it might be.
unknowns: Whether the controller has a job interface or only a panel.
Who may load software when the engineer is absent.
Whether this equipment is in scope of the machinery rules from 20 January 2027.
research_questions: What share of tags are safety functions?
How often does the first bench test fail?

already_counted.description: Engineer rewrites a routine draft that failed the tag check
Bench time stays with the engineer
The load at the panel stays with the engineer

incremental.description: Add a routine pattern only after the same non-safety pattern has passed the bench twice

approvals.approved_version: input-output list with safety flags marked
control software version whose bench tests passed

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes almost every tag is safety or one-off, so the draft rarely fires and the engineer still writes the software. The high case assumes routine non-safety blocks draft cleanly, but safety code, the bench, the signature, and the load stay manual. No unattended load is treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Integrate electrical and renewable energy systems

steps.what: Send the renewable energy interface signals
Pair renewable signals with electrical systems tags

loop.output: proposed pairs plus an unmatched list
loop.check: Each pair cites one renewable signal id and one electrical tag that both exist
loop.stop: One pass, then leave unmatched ids on the exception list
loop.why_not_simpler: Signal names are not shared, so a fixed join misses aliases

steps.what: Copy combined efficiency figures from the log

loop.input: simulation log and the run id
loop.output: efficiency figures that match the log
loop.check: Each figure equals the value printed for that run id
loop.stop: If the log has no run id, leave the note blank and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed cell reference can copy a figure from the wrong case

steps.what: Agree the limits that integrate the two systems
Sign the integration limits and the interface list
File the signed integration list

tasks.design: The mechanical engineer sends renewable equipment id and interface signals on a {WORKFLOW} form. The electrical engineer keeps the limit and the protection setting. A {SPREADSHEET} proposes a pair only when both a renewable signal id and an electrical tag exist. Combined-run figures are copied from a simulation log into {DOCS} only when they match the log. The meeting that agrees the limits stays with the people. One signed interface list is filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Signal names differed across the two systems, and limits lived in meeting notes, so a list could not show which pair was real.
tasks.enabler_now: Both sides can carry an id, and a simulation log can carry a run id that a copied figure must match.
tasks.still_hard: A shared name is not a shared meaning, and protection limits are a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer sets the limits and the protection, and can refuse a pair that shares a name but not a meaning.

ambition.what: Re-sign the interface when a renewable rating changes, not only at the first design review

tasks.altitude: Matching names takes less hunting. The meeting and the limits stay. The engineer can leave an unmatched signal on the exception list.

reach.task: Correct a renewable signal the match rejected
reach.learn: Which signals have no electrical tag and which limits were signed

evidence.claim: Integration work is an interface list and a meeting about limits. The list can be checked for ids. The limits cannot be taken from a model.
Digest [S11] says an executable simulation call is not a correct result. A combined-run figure is copied only when it matches the log.
Digest [S12] and [S13] say a safety component in electricity can be high-risk AI. A model must not set protection or operating limits.

assumptions: Focal role is the electrical engineer. The task ends when a signed interface list is filed. Commissioning on site is a later task.

Input contract: renewable equipment id, signal id, electrical tag, direction, limit value, simulation run id. Producer of renewable signals is the mechanical engineer. The electrical engineer writes limits. Unmatched signals stay on an exception list.
A native join is tried first. The bounded read runs only for names that join rejects.
The coordination meeting stays with the person. Protection settings are typed by the engineer, not proposed by the draft.
unknowns: Whether the network operator must also sign the limits.
Which simulation log is the run of record.
Who owns signals that belong to a supplier package.
research_questions: What share of renewable signals has no electrical tag?
How often does the meeting change a limit after the simulation?

already_counted.description: Engineer reviews pairs the name match got wrong
Limit meeting stays with the engineer
Signature time stays with the engineer

incremental.description: Maintain signal aliases when a new equipment package arrives
Mechanical engineer fixes signals the match rejected

approvals.approved_version: interface list signed for this renewable connection

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes signal names do not match and there is no structured log, so the engineer still reconciles by hand. The high case assumes pairs and log figures copy cleanly, but the meeting and the signature stay. Site commissioning is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The electrical engineer stops copying load tables, parts, and tag lists, and keeps the week for protection, customer limits, and bench tests.
reach: The electrical technician receives a signed test log instead of a chat note.
The mechanical engineer can read the interface list that was actually signed.
skills_to_grow: Keep a protection setting as a field a person signs, not as a model output.
Treat a passing test log as the only software version that may be loaded.
Write an interface as equipment id, signal, and limit so two systems can be checked.
role.ambitious_version: Each renewable scheme has a signed interface list, a tested control version, and a load table that leaves blank rows blank.
